items.title: Public institutions must be open to questioning: Supreme Court Justice Vikram Nath
items.summary: Growing awareness of citizens' rights has raised expectations from public institutions, which must remain accountable for the power entrusted to them, Supreme Court Justice Vikram Nath recently said. People today are far more aware of their rights and of the institutions that govern them. This change was something that was long in coming… But this growing awareness also brings with it a quiet weight. Expectations rise, and rightly so. items.title: SEBI's Closing Auction Session: Compliance obligations behind a market structure reform
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India's Closing Auction Session ("CAS"), introduced by Circular HO/47/11/11(3)2025-MRD-POD2/I/2765/2026 dated January 16, 2026 ("Circular") and operative since August 3, 2026, replaces the volume-weighted average price methodology that has determined closing prices for equity stocks with active derivative contracts. The Circular has been issued in exercise of SEBI's powers under Section 11(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, read with Regulation 51 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) (Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations) Regulations, 2018, the general statutory basis SEBI relies on to protect investor interests and regulate the securities market through directions to exchanges and clearing corporations. It is worth noting at the outset that CAS is implemented entirely through this circular-and-directions route, not through an amendment to the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations or the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations. For practitioners advising on it, that distinction matters: there is no amended regulation to append to a compliance manual, only a circular whose obligations flow through exchange-level Standard Operating Procedures, which is precisely why the operational implementation deserves closer legal attention than a more conventional regulation amendment might. The change followed an unusually extended consultation process, running from an initial paper on December 5, 2024, through a revised proposal on August 22, 2025, incorporating feedback from the Secondary Market Advisory Committee, recognised exchanges, clearing corporations, and the Futures Industry Association. The extended timeline reflects the stakes involved. The closing price is not a peripheral data point; it anchors derivatives settlement, benchmark index computation, and mutual fund NAV calculation, and a distorted closing figure propagates across all three. items.title: US court accepts Trump government proposal to dismisses fraud charges against Gautam Adani but terms it "highly unusual"
items.summary: A United States court has dismissed securities and wire fraud charges against Indian industrialist and billionaire Gautam Adani and two other executives, bringing the criminal proceedings against them to an end. items.title: Dignity, Data and Privacy: An evaluation of State of Goa v. Tarun Tejpal from a privacy perspective
items.summary: The allegations date to November 2013, wherein Tarun Tejpal allegedly assaulted the survivor on two separate occasions inside a hotel lift in Goa. The victim confided in colleagues that same night, and a week later emailed a complaint to Tehelka’s Managing Editor, seeking an apology and an internal inquiry. Tejpal replied with two apology emails before the matter went public and an FIR was registered. The trial court acquitted him, but it did so not on the core facts, but on its own reading of the survivor’s character and morality, reaching a conclusion after permitting the annihilation of her privacy at the altar of cross-examination for finding the truth and preserving liberty. But the question is whose liberty, and how? A perusal of the order of the trial court makes the choice unmistakably evident. Faced with a tension between the accused’s liberty and the survivor’s privacy, the trial court chose the accused’s rights at every turn and buried the privacy of the victim. The trial court allowed the defence to trawl through her sexual history and past relationships and treated her composure after the assault as proof that no assault had occurred. It read its own morality into the record and dismissed Tejpal’s apologies as coerced, and converted inconsistencies in testimony given five years later into fatal contradictions. The High Court reversed the trial court on account of perversity and held that the trial court’s findings ran directly against the evidence and rested on assumptions about how a “real” victim behaves rather than on the record. The High Court demolished the “ideal victim” construct and condemned the trial court for allowing this invasive, humiliating excavation of the victim’s privacy through her purported past sexual history and private WhatsApp messages, and having weighed it all, it found her evidence not merely corroborated but of sterling quality. The High Court held that two emails in which Tejpal apologised for a “shameful lapse of judgment” could not be waved away as coerced, because nothing on record showed coercion, and it is in this setting that the judgment upholds the privacy of the victim. The approach of the High Court on various aspects of privacy: bodily, decisional, and informational, makes it a landmark. items.title: Bidadi township row: Police halt JD(S) padayatra, party announces mega protest on Aug 18
items.summary: The Janata Dal (Secular) on Monday, August 10, called off its padayatra against the proposed Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township (GBIT) project after police stopped the march near Kaniminike on the outskirts of Bengaluru. The party has now shifted the protest to Freedom Park on August 18, where it plans to hold a larger demonstration under the leadership of JD(S) patriarch and former Prime Minister HD Deve Gowda. The three-day padayatra, led by JD(S) youth wing president Nikhil Kumaraswamy and backed by the BJP, began at Byramangala near Bidadi on August 9. It was scheduled to cover around 38 km before reaching Freedom Park on August 11. On Monday, protesters reached Kaniminike using a service road instead of the Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway. After a lunch break, Nikhil and other leaders attempted to proceed towards the NICE Road junction via Challaghatta Metro station. Police stopped them, citing concerns over traffic congestion. An argument broke out between the protesters and police personnel, and some protesters allegedly pushed police officers and attempted to cross the barricades. A few protesters were detained, following which the JD(S) decided to call off the march. “There won’t be any march tomorrow. On August 18, there will be a massive protest at Freedom Park,” Nikhil said. He accused the Congress government of using the police to obstruct the agitation and said the party would continue to oppose the proposed acquisition of farmers’ land. The padayatra had drawn attention after 93-year-old Deve Gowda joined the protesters on Sunday at BGS Circle in Bidadi. Gowda attacked Chief Minister DK Shivakumar over the proposed township, accusing the government of jeopardising farmers’ livelihoods. “Why do you want to destroy the livelihood of the farmers here? For what purpose? Please tell us, Shivakumar,” Gowda said. He questioned the need to acquire agricultural land when several sites and houses in Bengaluru were reportedly lying vacant. Citing figures available with the Bengaluru Development Authority, Gowda claimed around 20,000 BDA sites remained vacant, apart from unoccupied sites in other layouts and constructed houses. Gowda also rejected the government's proposed compensation of more than Rs 3 crore per acre, arguing that farmers should not be forced to give up their land merely because they are offered money. Nikhil similarly rejected the compensation offer and said the government would not be able to persuade farmers to part with their land.

items.title: Wildlife department to probe origin of lar gibbon seen in Actor Vikram’s video
items.summary: Actor Chiyaan Vikram has drawn the attention of wildlife authorities and conservationists after sharing a video of himself interacting with a lar gibbon. The species is a threatened primate protected under international wildlife trade regulations. The video, which Vikram posted on social media, showed him playing with a well-grown lar gibbon. It quickly went viral, but also triggered questions over how the exotic animal came to be in a private setting in Chennai and whether its owner possesses the documents required to legally keep it. The lar gibbon, scientifically known as Hylobates lar, is native to Southeast Asia and is listed under Appendix I of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). The species is also classified as a Schedule IV animal under India's amended Wildlife Protection Act. Under CITES, Appendix I covers species facing the highest level of protection and places stringent restrictions on international commercial trade. Possession of an exotic animal in India can also be subject to domestic requirements concerning its acquisition, registration, transfer and supporting documentation. The presence of a lar gibbon in a private setting, therefore, does not by itself establish an offence. Authorities would need to determine how the animal entered the country, where it was obtained from and whether its possession is supported by the documents and permissions required under applicable wildlife laws. Chennai wildlife warden Kulal Yogesh Vilas, speaking to Times of India, said the wildlife department would verify the animal's origin, including who it was procured from and whether the owner has documents establishing its purchase and possession. A forest ranger would be sent to conduct the verification, Yogesh Vilas said. The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau also said state wildlife authorities are generally asked to examine cases involving exotic pets and verify whether owners have valid documents and details about the source of the animals. The report added that V Thenmozhi, deputy director of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau's southern region, said authorities seek the assistance of state wildlife officials in such cases to check documentation and establish where an exotic animal was sourced. The video has also raised concerns among conservationists because of the way lar gibbons are captured and traded.
